key_insight: In a controlled wafer-map defect classification benchmark, the CV quantum neural network consistently outperforms the DV version, indicating that structured continuous-variable layers are better suited to capturing fine spatial defect patterns.
engineering_relevance: For semiconductor yield screening, the result suggests CV-based quantum heads may be the more promising paradigm for practical defect classification, especially on localized defect classes like Edge-Loc.
method: Shared ~4.3M-parameter convolutional backbone with interchangeable heads
Compared classical dense, CV-QNN, and DV-QNN heads under identical conditions
Scaled quantum heads to 3, 4, and 8 qumodes/qubits and evaluated on WM-811K
evidence_signal: On WM-811K eight-class wafer-map classification, the 4-qumode CV head reached 79.7±1.8% accuracy versus 61.6±1.4% for DV, while Edge-Loc recall was 0.66±0.06 for CV and ≤0.05 for DV.
watch_item: Both quantum heads still underperform the classical baseline and the reported advantage depends on the chosen low Fock cutoff and controlled experimental setup.
paper_title: Bridging Quantum Computing Paradigms toward Semiconductor Yield: A Controlled CV-versus-DV Comparison on Wafer-Map Defect Classification
